clips.text: For thousands of years, we have dreamed of minds made by human hands.
Bronze giants in Greek myth.
Clockwork figures that played music and wrote letters.
And in 1843, Ada Lovelace imagined an engine that could weave algebra, the way a loom weaves flowers.
clips.say: And in eighteen forty-three, Ada Lovelace imagined an engine that could weave algebra, the way a loom weaves flowers.

clips.text: In 1943, Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts showed that simple switches, wired like neurons, could compute logic.
clips.say: In nineteen forty-three, Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts showed that simple switches, wired like neurons, could compute logic.

clips.text: The artificial neuron was born.
In 1950, Alan Turing proposed a test.
clips.say: In nineteen fifty, Alan Turing proposed a test.

clips.text: If a machine could talk so well that we couldn't tell it from a person, could we still say it doesn't think?
In the summer of 1956, a workshop at Dartmouth College gave the dream its name.
clips.say: In the summer of nineteen fifty-six, a workshop at Dartmouth College gave the dream its name.

clips.text: Artificial intelligence.
Its founders believed every aspect of learning could be described so precisely that a machine could simulate it.
They thought real progress could be made in a single summer.
Two years later, Frank Rosenblatt unveiled the Perceptron, a machine that learned to recognize patterns on its own.
Newspapers predicted it would one day walk, talk, and be conscious of its own existence.
In 1966, a program called ELIZA imitated a psychotherapist.
clips.say: In nineteen sixty-six, a program called Eliza imitated a psychotherapist.

clips.text: It understood nothing.
Yet its creator's own secretary asked him to leave the room, so she could talk to it in private.
But the promises outran the machines.
Computers were too slow, the world too complex, and the funding froze.
The first AI winter had begun.
In the 1980s, expert systems brought a brief thaw.
clips.say: In the nineteen-eighties, expert systems brought a brief thaw.

clips.text: Then, a second winter set in.
Through the long cold, a few researchers kept faith in neural networks.
In 1986, they popularized backpropagation, a way for networks to learn from their own mistakes.
clips.say: In nineteen eighty-six, they popularized backpropagation, a way for networks to learn from their own mistakes.

clips.text: Soon, Yann LeCun's networks were reading handwritten digits on envelopes.
In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue defeated the world chess champion, Garry Kasparov.
clips.say: In nineteen ninety-seven, IBM's Deep Blue defeated the world chess champion, Garry Kasparov.

clips.text: It could examine two hundred million positions every second.
But chess was all it could do.
Then, three forces collided.
Oceans of data from the internet.
Graphics chips built for video games.
And networks deeper than ever before.
In 2012, a network called AlexNet crushed the ImageNet challenge, created by Fei-Fei Li and her team.
clips.say: In twenty twelve, a network called Alex Net crushed the Image Net challenge, created by Fei-Fei Lee and her team.

clips.text: The deep learning revolution had begun.
In 2016, DeepMind's AlphaGo challenged Lee Sedol, one of the greatest Go players of all time.
clips.say: In twenty sixteen, Deep Mind's Alpha Go challenged Lee Sedol, one of the greatest Go players of all time.

clips.text: Go has more possible positions than there are atoms in the universe.
In game two, on move thirty-seven, AlphaGo played a move no human would have played.
clips.say: In game two, on move thirty-seven, Alpha Go played a move no human would have played.

clips.text: Commentators thought it was a mistake.
It was brilliant.
AlphaGo won the match, four games to one.
clips.say: Alpha Go won the match, four games to one.

clips.text: In 2017, eight researchers at Google published a paper with a bold title: Attention Is All You Need.
clips.say: In twenty seventeen, eight researchers at Google published a paper with a bold title: Attention Is All You Need.

clips.text: Their Transformer could weigh every word against every other word, all at once.
And it scaled.
Language models grew from millions of parameters to billions.
They learned to write, to translate, and to code.
Then, on November 30th, 2022, ChatGPT put that power into everyone's hands.
clips.say: Then, on November thirtieth, twenty twenty-two, Chat G P T put that power into everyone's hands.

clips.text: One hundred million people tried it within two months.
Since then, the pace has only quickened.
AI now writes and paints, speaks and sees.
It has predicted the shapes of nearly every known protein.
In 2024, its pioneers received Nobel Prizes in physics and chemistry.
clips.say: In twenty twenty-four, its pioneers received Nobel Prizes in physics and chemistry.

clips.text: It solves olympiad mathematics, writes software, and more and more, it acts on our behalf.
More than seventy years ago, Alan Turing asked whether machines could think.
We are still debating the answer.
But a new question now belongs to all of us.
